name: Rimonabant
summary: Rimonabant, sold under the brand names Acomplia and Zimulti, is an anorectic antiobesity drug approved in Europe in 2006 but was withdrawn worldwide in 2008 due to serious neurological and psychiatric side effects; it was never approved in the United States. Rimonabant is an inverse agonist for the cannabinoid receptor CB1 and was first-in-class.

pharmacology.text: Rimonabant is an inverse agonist of the cannabinoid CB1 receptor. Originally thought to be selective for the CB1 receptor, rimonabant was subsequently also found to act as an antagonist of the μ-opioid receptor. These properties may make this drug useful in cases of cannabinoid or opioid overdose but more research and safety testing is required.

uses.text: Rimonabant was approved and used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes before being withdrawn from the market.

sideEffects.text: Data from clinical trials submitted to regulatory authorities showed that rimonabant caused depressive disorders or mood alterations in up to 10% of subjects and suicidal ideation in around 1%, and in Europe it was contraindicated for people with any psychiatric disorder, including clinical depression.

fact.en: Rimonabant did the opposite of cannabis at the CB1 receptor, and it reduced appetite. It was withdrawn in 2008 because it caused depression and suicidal thoughts in some users.
